> - Provenance: For every catalog entry we store source repo (commit SHA), model artifact SHA256, build config, quantization profile, and a reproducible container manifest.
> - Hash verification: We generate and publish signed checksums for served artifacts (Ed25519 signatures), plus a public key thumbprint for audit.
> - Pinning: Customers can pin at three levels: (a) model family + semantics (e.g., gpt-2-style), (b) explicit artifact (SHA256), (c) runtime variant (quantized/FP16). Pinning is sticky and route-level; rollout config can override.
> - Update notifications: We support webhook and email notifications for new model variants. For major semantic updates we recommend a 30-day notice window; minor patches 72 hours.
> - Rollback: Automatic rollback is supported when custom metrics (latency, hallucination rate, A/B eval score) breach configured thresholds for N consecutive windows. Rollbacks revert to the prior pinned artifact and can be gated by human approval.

Diego — draft bullets for the RFI package below. I focused on the procurement/legal friendly language and included SLAs where appropriate. Please review and let me know if we should expand any section into an appendix.

Draft RFI answers (to be included in RFI_Answer_NovaBank_20260804.pdf):

1) Model catalog & provenance
- We publish a machine-readable catalog export (CSV/JSON) containing: model_id, artifact_sha256, source_repo (when allowed), training-data-tag, allowed_licenses, build_date, quantization_profile, and version_label. We can provide on-demand signed exports for audits.
- Artifacts are accompanied by Ed25519-signed checksums and a catalog-level manifest (SBOM-style) that enumerates dependencies.

2) Version pinning and deployment controls
- Route-level pinning: customers can pin a specific artifact SHA or a version label per API key or route. Pinning is enforced in the runtime and cannot be superseded except by an authorized admin request.
- Rollouts: canary percentages, time-based ramps, and explicit approval gates.

3) Update notifications and windows
- Major semantic updates (behavioral / API changes): 30 days advance notification via webhook and email; a human-confirmed migration plan is recommended.
- Minor patches (non-semantic, security/bugfixes): 72-hour notice when changes affect artifact binary or runtime behavior.

4) Automated rollback and health monitoring
- Health policy: customers define custom metric thresholds (e.g., top-line metric, hallucination rate, latency). The platform continuously evaluates these metrics and will automatically revert to the previous pinned artifact if thresholds are breached for 3 consecutive evaluation windows.
- MTTR expectations: automated rollback + reconverge typically < 10 minutes; notification and detailed incident report within 60 minutes.

5) Licensing & provenance for open models
- We track upstream license metadata for every catalog entry and record license changes as events. If an upstream license becomes incompatible with a customer’s profile (e.g., moves to a copyleft license), we flag affected customers within 24 hours and provide remediation options (pin to previous artifact, migrate to alternative model, or remove serving artifact).
- We provide exportable license attestations for models served to a customer and can add a clause to enterprise contracts requiring notice of upstream license changes.

6) Audit artifacts we can supply
- Signed catalog export (CSV/JSON), artifact checksums (Ed25519 sigs), SBOM-style manifest, model provenance logs, and deployment / rollout history for the requested timeframe.

Attachments: Redwood_Rollback_Strategy_v1.pdf (internal runbook), Model_Catalog_Schema.csv (catalog fields).

Let me know if you want a brief cover note summarizing mitigation options for license drift. I can add one.

—Marissa Cole
